blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Local stocks fell to their lowest close in more than six years on Monday as investors grappled with rising stagflation risks at home and the prospect of another US interest rate hike. The benchmark Philippine Stock Exchange Index (PSEi) dropped 2 percent, or 111.61 points, to close at 5,481.88. READ: The Philippines’ stagflation-lite moment It was the index’s weakest finish since May 18, 2020, when it closed at 5,479.35, according to Philstocks Financial Inc. The brokerage said elevated inflation and slowing economic growth weighed on investor sentiment. Luis Limlingan, head of sales at Regina Capital Development Corp., said […]...
